rows.note: Use this as the everyday broad choice for a poor, run-down urban area when the ethnic dimension is not the focus.

example.english: That area used to be a ghetto, and it still has many old buildings.
example.traditional: 嗰區以前係貧民窟，而家仲有好多舊樓。
example.jyutping: go2 keoi1 ji5 cin4 hai6 pan4 man4 fat1 ji4 gaa1 zung6 jau5 hou2 do1 gau6 lau4

rows.note: Use this when the defining point is that a particular ethnic group is concentrated in the area, even if poverty is not foregrounded.

example.english: This ghetto has preserved many local traditions.
example.traditional: 呢個族裔聚居區保留咗好多當地傳統。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 zuk6 jeoi6 zeoi6 geoi1 keoi1 bou2 lau4 zo2 hou2 do1 dong1 dei6 cyun4 tung2

rows.note: Use this specifically for a Jewish quarter, especially in historical descriptions of forced segregation.

example.english: During Nazi rule, residents of the ghetto could not move in and out freely.
example.traditional: 納粹統治期間，猶太人區入面嘅居民冇得自由出入。
example.jyutping: naap6 seoi3 tung2 zi6 kei4 gaan1 jau4 taai3 jan4 keoi1 jap6 min6 ge3 geoi1 man4 mou5 dak1 zi6 jau4 ceot1 jap6
